transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net mobile customer care, my name is Callum. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Callum. I just landed at Heathrow Terminal 2 from a twelve-hour flight from Singapore, my phone is displaying 'No SIM card installed', and I have no way to contact my family or order a taxi to get home! I am completely stranded in the arrivals hall with my luggage!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you provide your registered mobile telephone number and your billing address so I can pull up your account profile?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My mobile number is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero five one eight, and the address is 14 Windsor Walk, Reading, RG1 3DD.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the four-digit security PIN on your mobile account, Avery?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those account credentials, Avery. I have your subscriber profile open on our mobile cellular network portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to summarize what you are experiencing: upon landing from your flight at Heathrow, your handset began displaying a 'No SIM card installed' alert, and neither reseating the physical nano-SIM nor rebooting the device has restored cellular connectivity. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly the problem. The phone had full 5G in Singapore before boarding, but as soon as I took it off Airplane Mode here at Heathrow, it went straight to No SIM.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you physically ejected the SIM tray using a paperclip or SIM ejector tool to inspect the physical copper contacts?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I borrowed an earring from another passenger, popped the tray out, blew on the chip, and slotted it back in, but it still says No SIM.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you notice any visible diagonal scratches, oxidization, or physical cracking across the gold microchip pads?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is a slight hairline scratch across the center copper contact pad where the tray guide slides across it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are you traveling with a traveling companion whose mobile handset you could test your SIM card inside?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I am traveling alone on business, so I don't have another spare smartphone with me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me on hold for about thirty-five seconds while I query the Home Location Register to check your SIM card's IMSI authentication status.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Avery. The cellular core network register shows your IMSI registration has been marked inactive due to multiple unrecoverable cryptographic handshake failures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that mean the physical microchip has suffered electrical failure?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, when the internal integrated circuit microprocessor on a nano-SIM degrades, the baseband modem cannot read the subscriber encryption keys.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you dispatch a replacement nano-SIM to the airport or activate an electronic eSIM profile for me right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Replacement physical SIM cards are dispatched via Royal Mail second class from our central logistics depot in Leeds, which takes three to five working days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Three to five working days?! I am standing in the middle of Heathrow Airport right now trying to get home to Reading!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our postal fulfillment process cannot deliver physical envelopes to airport arrival terminals.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can't you send me an instant digital eSIM QR code to my email so I can download a digital profile immediately?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Company security policy dictates that instant eSIM profile activation can only be initiated by logging into your web account dashboard from a registered desktop computer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My desktop computer is sitting in my study at home fifty miles away! I need internet and phone service right now so I can book a car home!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will have to walk over to an airport electronics kiosk in Terminal 2 and purchase a temporary third-party pay-as-you-go tourist SIM card yourself.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why should I pay thirty pounds to an airport tourist vendor for an overpriced SIM when I pay S-Net forty pounds every month for unlimited mobile service?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hardware chip failures that occur while traveling internationally must be managed through local terminal retail facilities.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can't you at least call an S-Net supervisor to manually override the desktop verification requirement and email the eSIM QR code to my iPad?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our customer care tier two systems enforce two-factor authentication, which transmits a verification SMS to your registered SIM, which is currently unreadable.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So your security system won't let me activate a new SIM because it wants to text the dead SIM?! That is a completely absurd Catch-22 loop!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The security protocol is designed to prevent fraudulent unauthorized SIM-swap identity theft.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand SIM-swap prevention, but surely you have an alternative email verification pathway for authenticated account holders stranded abroad!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The email fallback authorization pathway requires visiting a company retail high street store with photographic passport identification.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there an S-Net retail high street store located inside Heathrow Terminal 2?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, our nearest retail store is located on Hounslow High Street, approximately four miles outside the airport perimeter.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How am I supposed to get to Hounslow without working navigation or taxi apps on my phone?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can connect your handset to the complimentary Heathrow Airport Wi-Fi network to use web browsing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The free airport Wi-Fi disconnects every twenty minutes and won't authenticate with my corporate ride-hailing app!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you provided earlier, Avery, your registered contact number on file is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero five one eight?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero five one eight, as I told you when the call started.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have ordered a replacement physical nano-SIM to 14 Windsor Walk, Reading, RG1 3DD via standard post.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you serious?! I've been standing in the cold arrivals hall for forty-five minutes trying to fix this, my phone battery is at four percent, and now you tell me I have to buy another SIM card or wait five days?! This is outrageous service!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Delivery timelines for replacement postal SIMs are governed by Royal Mail second-class dispatch schedules.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You are offering zero practical help to a stranded customer!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have provided the terminal retail options and logged the postal SIM replacement order under ticket reference SIM-77291.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What good is a ticket reference when my battery is dying in two minutes?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The order is queued in the fulfillment database.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am going to file an official complaint with Ofcom as soon as I get home.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are entitled to raise a formal customer dissatisfaction case via our online portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least apply a credit to cover the cost of the tourist SIM I'm being forced to buy?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Third-party merchant retail purchases cannot be reimbursed onto mobile billing accounts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unbelievable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our network coverage across the UK remains at ninety-nine percent once a working SIM is installed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Your 5G coverage is usually very fast in Reading when the SIM card actually works, but right now I have nothing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The replacement nano-SIM will restore full 5G mobile data access once it arrives at your home address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Callum, if the kiosk SIM doesn't work, what should I...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There is nothing more I can do from here today while you are in the terminal. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Avery. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Callum? He hung up on me!
